subject: POC follow-up: auth/routing + response schema / streaming questions
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Subject: POC follow-up: auth/routing + response schema / streaming questions

Hi Liam / Asha — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for the POC: 

Summary of call
- Goal: integrate Redwood inference for in-product summarization + reranking pipeline; target latency < 250ms p90 for single-turn queries, embedding-based search for reranker.
- Scope for POC: SDK bootstrapping, auth setup (dev -> staging -> prod), routing policy (region + cost fallback), baseline schema for chat responses (structured metadata + tool call hooks), and streaming behaviour for progressive UI.

Open items we promised to validate
1) Auth: dev API keys vs mTLS for staging/prod. You asked about a migration path and how tokens can be rotated without downtime.
2) Routing: primary region = us-west, fallback to us-east; want specifics on sticky session behaviour for KV cache and model variant fallback.
3) Structured output/tool-calling: sample response contract for our reranker pipeline (how to encode candidate scores + provenance).
4) Chat vs completions: recommended model patterns for short Q/A vs multi-turn assistants and tokenization implications.
5) Streaming semantics: partial responses + stop sequence handling for our UI incremental render.

Next steps (proposed)
- Karthik + Ben to produce a short tech note (attached) that shows API snippets for: SDK initialisation, API key rotation pattern, and region routing config. (ETA EOD today)
- Redwood to provide a sample response schema (JSON contract) with an example tool-calling payload for a rerank operation. (ETA tomorrow)
- NovusAI to share a small sample payload (1k characters typical query) so we can simulate tokenization and cost.

I've attached a short matrix (poc-auth-matrix.xlsx) and a working draft (20270930-novusai-poc-multi-region-mp.md) describing routing choices.

Thanks — Grace

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Liam Patel <liam@novusai.com>, Asha Rao <asha@novusai.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 14:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC follow-up: auth/routing + response schema / streaming questions

Thanks for the summary, Grace — adding technical detail below so NovusAI can evaluate trade-offs. Marking the items from the call.

1) Auth (dev -> staging -> prod)
- Dev: short-lived API keys issued from the console.
- Staging: recommend integrating with your IdP + short-lived keys minted by a CI role; we support scoped API keys (read-only vs inference) and key rotation via the API — rotation can be zero-downtime if you pre-provision the new key and switch clients over (we support key aliasing for phased rollouts).
- Prod: for higher security we support mTLS (customer-managed certs) + mutual auth at the transport layer. Alternative is KMS-wrapped API keys + HSM for signing.
- Action item: which approach do you prefer for prod? If mTLS, we'll send the cert provisioning guide.

2) Routing and cache affinity
- If you set region priority {us-west, us-east}, requests route to the first available region. For latency-critical paths you can pin to a region (sticky) per client id; that preserves KV cache warmness for session-scoped models.
- Fallback: when a region is saturated we gracefully route to the cheaper model variant (same architecture but lower context length / quantized) — appetite for quality degradation must be set in the routing policy.
- Note: cross-region KV cache misses will increase token cost on the cold path. We'll include a small simulation in the doc.

3) Response schema + tool calling
- Proposed minimal contract (we'll attach formal JSON): top-level fields {text, tokens, model_version, tools: [ {name, args, score, provenance}] , structured: {entities:[], reranker: {candidates: [{id, score, snippet, embedding_ref}]}}.
- Tool-calling: we support two modes — inline tool hints (client calls external tool) and direct execution (Redwood calls verified tool endpoints). For reranking, prefer inline hints with embedding references, then do a separate reranker call to keep inference costs predictable.

4) Chat vs completions, tokenization & stop sequences
- Chat: best for conversational state and tool-calling; uses messages[] format and maintains per-session KV cache. Recommended when you need assistant-like multi-turn.
- Completions: cheaper for single-shot generation; use when you only need final text and no tool call orchestration.
- Tokenization: model-specific. For the models we'll propose, tokenization average is ~0.75 tokens per char for english prose — we'll run your sample to get exact counts. 
- max_tokens: set the hard ceiling for generation. For streaming you can still set max_tokens — streaming will end early when a stop is encountered.
- stop sequences: client-side stop handling is supported; we stream tokens until stop thresholds and then close the stream. For multi-byte or token-boundary stops we recommend specifying both character and token stops if determinism is critical.

5) Streaming semantics (UI incremental render)
- We stream partial tokens as they are generated. Each event contains token, cum_tokens, and partial_json when structured output is used. For tool-calling: we emit a tool_call_started event, then tool_call_output chunks, then tool_call_completed.
- If you need guaranteed linebreak alignment in the UI, buffer by newline events — we can add a newline-aware flush in the SDK.

I attached a small cURL + Node snippet in the shared doc. Ben / Grace: I can also produce a minimal SDK example that demonstrates: API key rotation, region pinning, and streaming incremental parsing.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: POC follow-up: auth/routing + response schema / streaming questions

Thanks Karthik — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 
- For prod we prefer not to manage mTLS ourselves; we'd prefer KMS-wrapped API keys + HSM-backed signing if Redwood supports an HSM integration for key storage.
- Our UI needs partial tokens to render in <200ms chunks; is newline buffering something we can enable per-client?
- Reranker: we want the candidate list to include per-token provenance for highlights (start/end offsets) — will that blow up token payload sizes?
- Also, can you provide an example of the cheaper fallback model quality loss? Our product manager wants a sample prompt that shows the same query on the primary model vs fallback quantized variant so they can decide tolerance.

We'll share a 1k-character sample payload and our expected p90 latency targets by EOD. Also, please send the cert provisioning guide only if we decide to go with mTLS.

Best,
Liam
Director of Product, NovusAI
liam@novusai.com
